rounds.text: D.P. Abhushan Ltd demonstrates exceptional fundamental capital efficiency, evidenced by a robust 34.5% ROE [E7] and a 24.4% ROCE [E6], significantly outperforming the sector median ROCE of 9.9% [E60]. This superior efficiency translates into high operational momentum, with compounded sales growth reaching 42% and compounded profit growth hitting 48% over the trailing twelve months [E8, E9]. Retail execution is exceptionally sharp, highlighted by stable store conversion rates of 82% to 83% [E74] and a same-store sales growth rate of approximately 20% [E75]. Furthermore, management has laid out ambitious yet clear top-line expansion targets of INR 4,800 crores for FY27 and INR 5,500 crores for FY28 [E61], supported by a strong sectoral tailwind in Consumer Durables with a score of +0.80 [E57]. Conceded: the stock trades at an elevated P/E of 81.4 [E1] and price-to-book of 23.27 [E2], alongside a weak cash conversion ratio of 0.41x for Mar 2022 [E18].

The current market price of D.P. Abhushan Ltd is disconnected from its fundamental intrinsic value, sitting at a steep multiple of 81.4x P/E and 23.27x P/B [E1, E2]. A discounted cash flow model explicitly flags an intrinsic value of Rs 408 per share compared to a market price of Rs 1,443, resulting in an extreme negative margin of safety of -253.7% [E29, E30]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that today's price aggressively demands a 27.5% earnings growth rate, far outstripping the base case assumption of 10.0% [E31]. Conceded: the company displays an impressive ROE of 34.5% and a solid 3-year median ROE of 31% [E7, E13]. However, this profitability fails to convert cleanly into liquidity, evidenced by a weak cash conversion ratio of 0.41x and operating cash flow representing only 40% of operating profit in March 2022 [E18, E21]. Finally, leverage remains a pressing structural risk, with a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.23x and total borrowings resting at Rs 170 Cr in March 2022 [E22, E23].

Conceded: the discounted cash flow model gives an intrinsic value of Rs 408 and a negative margin of safety [E29, E30]. However, relying solely on static DCF outputs ignores the explosive reality of the company's fundamentals, including a 42% compounded sales growth and a 48% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E8, E9]. Conceded: the P/E sits at 81.4x and the price-to-book is 23.27x [E1, E2]. Yet these premium multiples are backed by elite capital efficiency, demonstrated by an ROCE of 24.4% and an ROE of 34.5% that significantly outpace the sector median ROCE of 9.9% [E6, E7, E60]. Conceded: cash conversion was 0.41x in March 2022 [E18]. Nevertheless, the company generated tangible liquidity with Rs 17 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 9 Cr in free cash flow, alongside management's commitment to fund expansions through internal accruals rather than long-term debt [E19, E20, E77]. Finally, while debt-to-equity is 1.23x [E22], the business operates in a thriving sector tailwind of +0.80 and is scaling rapidly toward management's long-term retail and revenue targets [E57, E61, E63].

Conceded: the company posted 42% compounded sales growth and 48% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E8, E9], alongside an ROCE of 24.4% and an ROE of 34.5% that exceed sector medians [E6, E7, E60]. However, these historical growth metrics clash directly with current operational reality, as the screen highlights a recent 26% year-over-year sales drop and decelerating earnings growth [E51, E52]. Conceded: the business generated Rs 17 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 9 Cr in free cash flow [E19, E20], and management plans to fund expansion via internal accruals [E77]. Yet a cash conversion ratio of just 0.41x reveals that reported profits are running far ahead of actual cash collection, pointing to hidden risks in receivables and accruals [E18]. Conceded: the Consumer Durables sector enjoys a positive tailwind of +0.80 [E57]. Nevertheless, leverage remains a structural vulnerability with a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.23x and borrowings sitting at Rs 170 Cr [E22, E23], all while institutional money flow turns negative as institutional holdings drop [E28].

Conceded: the screen highlights a recent 26% year-over-year sales drop and decelerating earnings growth [E51, E52]. However, this short-term reading is completely contradicted by the trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 42% and compounded profit growth of 48% [E8, E9], alongside robust same-store sales growth reaching approximately 20% YoY [E75]. Conceded: cash conversion stands at 0.41x for Mar 2022 [E18], but this operational snapshot delivered tangible absolute figures of Rs 17 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 9 Cr in free cash flow [E19, E20], while management intends to execute future expansion fully through internal accruals [E77]. Conceded: debt-to-equity is 1.23x with borrowings at Rs 170 Cr [E22, E23], and institutional holdings show a slight negative shift [E28]. Nonetheless, borrowings remained virtually flat, moving merely from Rs 169 Cr to Rs 170 Cr year-on-year [E23], and management explicitly has no current plans for long-term borrowings while anticipating finance costs to decrease gradually through GML, futures hedging, and leasing [E72, E78].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth reached 42% and compounded profit growth hit 48% [E8, E9], and same-store sales growth reached approximately 20% YoY [E75]. However, the bull minimizes that earnings growth is actively decelerating alongside a recent 26% year-over-year sales drop [E51, E52]. Conceded: operating cash flow was Rs 17 Cr and free cash flow was Rs 9 Cr in Mar 2022 [E19, E20]. Yet the bull ignores that this produced a weak cash conversion ratio of just 0.41x, meaning reported profits far outpaced actual cash generation and pointed directly to rising receivables and accruals [E18, E21]. Conceded: borrowings only inched from Rs 169 Cr to Rs 170 Cr [E23] and management has no current long-term borrowing plans [E78]. Nonetheless, debt-to-equity remains elevated at 1.23x, meaning total debt exceeds net worth and creates tangible leverage risk [E22]. Furthermore, the bull fails to address that the proposed QIP had to be put on hold entirely due to unfavorable market conditions [E76], leaving the company vulnerable while institutional money flow registers negative [E28].
